exercises.title: Digital Communication Protocols: concept check
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Why does an I²C bus need pull-up resistors?
choices: They limit the clock to 100 kHz
I²C is differential and needs them for balance
Devices only pull the lines low (open-drain), so resistors provide the high level
They terminate reflections like a CAN bus
hints: No device drives the line high.

exercises.title: Digital Communication Protocols: worked analysis
exercises.instructionMarkdown:
Decode representative UART, SPI, I2C, and CAN captures and identify one fault in each.

Show assumptions, equations, units, standard-value choices, ratings, tolerance effects, and the measurements that would verify the result.
checklist: I drew or described the complete source and return path.
I carried units and checked the order of magnitude.
I checked ratings and at least one worst-case condition.
I wrote an observable verification step before viewing the solution.
hints: Start with a symbolic relationship before substituting numbers.
Separate typical behavior from guaranteed limits and add measurement tolerance.
exercises.solutionMarkdown:
## Reference solution

UART is asynchronous and decoded from idle level, start bit, data order, optional parity, and stop bits. SPI requires correct clock polarity/phase and chip-select framing. I²C uses open-drain lines, pull-ups, addresses, ACK/NACK, and repeated starts. CAN requires differential wiring, arbitration, bit timing, and one termination at each physical bus end.

The governing principle is: **interpret electrical layer, timing, framing, ownership, and error recovery together**. Define every reference direction and convert values to coherent SI units. Compare the result with component ratings and standard available values, then report a bounded expectation that includes tolerance, temperature, supply variation, and instrument loading.

### Verification evidence

1. Power off and confirm wiring, polarity, and discharge state.
2. Configure a conservative current limit.
3. Predict source current and the critical node voltages or waveform features.
4. Power on and compare the first measurement with the bounded prediction.
5. Stop if current, temperature, smell, or waveform exceeds the safe bound.

The notebook should make both the reasoning and bench test independently reproducible.

exercises.title: Digital Communication Protocols: measurement and fault investigation
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Plan or perform a low-voltage investigation of **voltage standard confused with protocol, missing common reference, wrong SPI mode, CAN termination absent**. Record a safe setup, predicted healthy evidence, observed evidence, one hypothesis at a time, and the final verification.
checklist: I documented the de-energized inspection and safe current limit.
I recorded expected healthy readings before measuring.
I used one falsifiable hypothesis at a time.
I included final evidence that distinguishes cause from symptom.
hints: Measure the supply current and block boundaries before probing internal details.
Change only one condition between measurements.
